items.prompt: How confident are you that you could explain the difference between structured, semi-structured and unstructured information?
An 80-page annual report is uploaded as one PDF. Which form of information is it?

options.label: Unstructured — the system receives one file and does not automatically understand the paragraphs inside
Structured — the document contains names and dates
Semi-structured — it was sent through an API

items.explanation: The PDF arrives as a file whose contents the system cannot address as fields; the JSON-style varying document would be semi-structured and a fixed record would be structured.

items.prompt: A school club app holds many kinds of information. Give one realistic example of each form — structured, semi-structured and unstructured — and say why it belongs in that form.

criteria: Names one plausible example of each of the three forms
Correctly matches each example to structured, semi-structured or unstructured

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why having access to a file is not the same as understanding its contents.

criteria: States that the system receives a file without automatically knowing what is inside
Explains that something must extract structure before the contents become usable

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could explain how a database record about a file relates to the file itself in object storage?
Maya uploads a 90 MB annual-report PDF. What does the database store?

options.label: The 90 MB of PDF bytes inside the organization's row
A document record with the ID, owner, type and storage location of the file
One column per paragraph of the report

items.explanation: The database keeps facts about the file, including the pointer to it; the bytes live in object storage.

items.prompt: Sketch the document record a system would create when a student uploads a project photo. List at least four fields it should contain, and say where the photo itself lives.

criteria: Lists at least four fields such as document_id, owner or project ID, type and storage_location
States that the photo's bytes live in file or object storage, not inside the row

items.prompt: In your own words, explain what the database knows about an uploaded file versus what object storage holds.

criteria: Explains that the database stores facts about the file such as ID, owner, type and location
States that the file's bytes live in storage and the record points to them

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could match a search question to the right tool: database filter, keyword search or semantic search?
A user asks the system to find documents that mention the phrase food insecurity. Which retrieval tool fits best?

options.label: A database filter on exact field values
Keyword search over the text of documents

items.explanation: The question names specific words to find inside document text, which is exactly what keyword or full-text search does.

items.prompt: Write three questions a community-resources app might answer — one that needs a database filter, one that needs keyword search, and one that needs semantic search — and label each.

criteria: Provides one clear question per retrieval tool
Each question genuinely needs its labeled tool rather than any of the three

items.prompt: In your own words, explain the difference between keyword search and semantic search, and give an example where keyword search fails.

criteria: Explains that keyword search matches words while semantic search matches meaning
Gives an example where different words with the same meaning defeats keyword search

items.prompt: How confident are you that you could trace what happens between a user uploading a PDF and the AI answering a question about it?
In the upload-and-ask pipeline, what happens immediately before the AI generates its answer?

options.label: The entire document collection is sent to the model
Search and retrieval pick the strongest passages, which are given to the model with the question
The PDF is converted back into a database row

items.explanation: Find first, generate second: retrieval selects the relevant sections and places them into the model's context with the question.

items.prompt: List the stages between a user uploading a report and the AI answering a question about it, in order, from storage to the generated answer.

criteria: Includes storing the file, creating a record, extracting text, chunking and indexing
Ends with search or retrieval feeding the relevant passages to the AI

items.prompt: In your own words, explain why the system retrieves relevant passages first instead of sending every document to the AI.

criteria: Mentions scale, cost or speed as reasons not to send everything
Explains that retrieval delivers the small relevant subset the AI actually needs
